newsitem.title: UK: Heady LME zinc spurs jump in option volatility.
newsitem.headline: Heady LME zinc spurs jump in option volatility.

text.p: A scramble for LME zinc options by players fearing sharp prices swings in coming months sent implied volatility surging this week, traders said.
A combination of speculators, market makers and Chinese smelters have been buying both calls and puts, they added.
"This market is not going to sit still. It could go up another $100 or fall $300. You want to buy gamma," one said.

Chinese smelters, said to be short by up to 250,000 tonnes, was thought to have bought 400-500 lots (equivalent to 10,000-12,500 tonnes) of calls from a large U.S. investment bank this week, one trader said.
Speculators have been buying calls and puts all over the map, with at-the-money (ATM) options changing hands as well as strikes above and below the market from $1,400 up to $1,700.
Nearby implied volatility traded as high as 32 percent, up from about 24.5 percent a week ago, traders said.
"It's crazy. These vols are getting carried away," one said.

The heated volatility was sparking nervousness, with another dealer saying he had quoted options several times on Friday morning but had sold none. "The market is dangerous, I'm trying to quote as little as possible."
August ATM implied volatility was quoted as high as 32.0/36.0 percent on Friday morning, and September at 30.0/33.0 percent by some dealers, while others had them one or two points lower.
The jump in implied volatility compared to historic volatility at 16.7 percent, which has held little changed this month and fallen from a peak of nearly 20 percent in May.

Speculative buying on the back of tightness centred in September swept LME three month prices to fresh seven-year highs of $1,600 Friday morning, given a boost by panic short-covering by short option grantors.
But once the September tightness dissipates, many players are expecting a sharp fall in prices.
"People are expecting the market to drop, they are looking to buy 25 percent delta puts nearby," a dealer said.
Any tumble in underlying prices would snowball as option grantors liquidate hedges and speculators rush to take profits.

Aluminium volatility also gained this week, with August trading up to 22.0 percent implied volatility, up about three points on the week. August ATM volatility was quoted at 20.0/23.0 percent and September at 19.5/21.5 percent.
Activity had also been seen for 1998, nudging up volatility for first half 1998 about a half a point to 17.0/18.5 percent.
Nearby ATM and upside call options were the main target, with strikes between $1,600 and $1,750, dealers said.
Copper volatility, however, edged down a couple of points as players offloaded material.
"Now that the backwardation has virtually disappeared, people are feeling a bit more comfortable with the market and they want to cut down on time decay," one trader said.
"It's general volatility selling," he added.
August was quoted at 19.0/21.0 percent and September at 21.5/23.0 percent.
Nickel volatility was up slightly with upside calls well bid for. August implied volatility was quoted at 22.5/25.5 percent and September at 24.0/26.0 percent.
Lead vols were slightly easier and tin was quiet.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
